proposal:
STATUS. Hand-derived; nothing executed; no Lean. This is an audit plus sound preprocessing. It is not polynomial SAT, gives no universal growth bound, and leaves residual search unbounded. The watcher handoff carries no statements and contributes nothing.

AUDIT OF v3 (read, not run). I found no soundness defect.
- Local-to-global: each quotient slice uses only forms supported inside its block, so the per-block table identity gives F(x)=G(Mx) for every x by conjunction. The counts partition all quotient clauses.
- Right inverse: all r^2 entries of MR=I are checked, so G(y)=G(MRy)=F(Ry).
- Skips: every skip returns the untouched input.

Findings:
(a) Verification is polynomial only under the width cap. It pays 2^|K| per block regardless of |Z_K|.
(b) Discovery cost is outside the 8M estimate. The greedy loop rebuilds basis(chosen+[v]) per candidate, about candidates*r^2 steps (my unmeasured estimate: 6.7e7 at 16384 candidates, r=64). An incremental echelon removes a factor r.
(c) The test 0<r<n rejects invertible width-reducing basis changes (r=n), although the same proof covers them.
(d) Parity blind spot, exact from the code. For full-parity blocks each annihilator is {0,f_K}. v3 compresses iff the f_K are independent and fewer than n. Every dependent system is labelled incompatible_greedy_basis (or no_dimension_reduction at rank n). Inconsistent parity systems are always dependent, so v3 never compresses one.

MECHANISM 1: KERNEL-SECTION. Let N be the set of t in GF(2)^n whose variable flip maps every clause of F to a clause of F. Equivalently t|K lies in W_K for every block, so N=(sum A_K)^perp and dim N=n-r with v3's r. Let J be an information set of N, with a basis in echelon form (identity on J).
Lemma: F is satisfiable iff F restricted by x_J=0 is.
Proof: given x, add the basis vectors selected by x_J. The result has x_J=0 and F is unchanged. Lifting is extension by zero.
Consequences:
- No compatibility condition. Incompatible only means greedy found no adapted basis; an r-variable quotient exists whenever r<n.
- No growth. Restriction never adds or widens clauses.
- Table-free certificate: generators and J, checked by clause lookup in O(dim N * total literals). No 2^|K| and no width cap.
- Discovery: W_K in |Z_K|^2 set operations, then A_K and N by elimination. Polynomial in input bits.
- Choice of J: information sets are matroid bases, so greedy by occurrence count maximises the literal occurrences removed.
- Versus v3: residual block width is |K minus J| >= d_K, with equality iff J meets K in an information set of W_K. v3's adapted basis can be strictly narrower. So run v3 first, section on skip, regroup supports, and repeat (at most n rounds).
This is classical phase-shift symmetry breaking. It is new only to this pipeline.

MECHANISM 2: ORBIT-COVER (extra clauses). Split F into F0 and H, with N computed from F0 alone. For C in H let rho(C) be the rank of N restricted to supp(C).
Lemma: if the sum over H of 2^-rho(C) is below 1, then F is satisfiable iff F0 is.
Proof: fix x satisfying F0. The t in N with C false at x+t form an affine subspace of density 2^-rho(C), or none. The union bound leaves a good t, and F0(x+t)=F0(x). Conditional expectations over a basis of N find t deterministically.
So a single extra clause meeting the kernel never changes satisfiability. This is a fibre-counting statement and only a sufficient condition. Discovery of the split is heuristic: put clauses whose N-orbit leaves F into H, otherwise freeze their supports.

WORK. Preprocessing and certificates are polynomial as above. The quotient is no larger than the input. Residual search is unbounded. Kernel-free formulas (N=0) gain nothing, for example full-rank parity of width 6, where IALH has no window.

FIXTURE (a labelled control, not a growth witness). Tseitin on the circulant C16(1,2): 16 vertices, 32 edges, charge 1 at one vertex, 128 width-4 clauses.
Pinned v3 predictions: compression skipped with incompatible_greedy_basis (16 forms, rank 15, block (15,16,30,32) holds the dependent form). IALH then refutes at the root from the 16 parity windows. Result: sat false, peak 0, no layers.
Independent section test with J={16..32}: 30 clauses on variables 1..15 (units [1] and [-15], 28 binary), refuted by unit propagation.
Larger family, peak unpredicted: Tseitin on the 6-regular C8(1,2,3), 24 variables, 256 clauses. v3 must skip as incompatible, root IALH has no window, and section gives a 7-variable tree instance.
missing_theorem:
T99 (first; Lean, general n, no sorry). SECTION: if F is closed under the clause flip of each listed generator and the generators are in echelon form on J, then F is satisfiable iff F restricted by x_J=0 is, with the explicit maps above. It needs no fibre counting and no tables, so it should be shorter than T94. It removes the incompatible case from the dimension question. Hand proof only.

T100 (Lean). ORBIT-COVER with the conditional-expectation lifting. A local-lemma strengthening (each clause depends only on generators meeting its support) is plausible, but I have not checked its hypotheses.

T101 (open; the exact theorem for arbitrary extra clauses). For N-invariant F0 and arbitrary H, decide whether some x satisfying F0 has an orbit not covered by the affine sets of H. With F0 empty and N everything this is CNF-SAT, so an unconditional theorem is polynomial SAT itself. Only conditional targets are provable: density below 1 (T100), or bounded rank of N on vars(H), where sectioning F directly leaves at most r+rank variables.

T102 (open; replaces T98). Incompatible spaces no longer block dimension reduction. What remains is width: decide whether some information set J, or any basis change, attains width d_K on every block at once, and find any handle on kernel-free formulas with nontrivial local stabilisers. ATOM-REFINE covers adapted bases only. I have no algorithm and no hardness proof.
self_attack:
1. Nothing here is new mathematics. SECTION is standard symmetry breaking and ORBIT-COVER is a union bound. Both are unexecuted hand proofs.
2. SECTION reaches the same dimension r as v3, never lower, and can leave wider blocks. Whether it reproduces the 2-CNF quotients of the 36- and 96-clause cases depends on a common information set, which I have not checked.
3. After sectioning, N=0. Every hard instance can be made kernel-free, so this says nothing about worst-case growth.
4. ORBIT-COVER is weak: at equal rank rho it tolerates at most 2^rho-1 extra clauses. The 36+9 and 96+6 cases may exceed density 1, and then it is silent. Split discovery is heuristic.
5. The fixture's peak 0 rests on SymPy HNF finding the mod-2 dual at the root. I cannot run it. If IALH misses, the peak is unknown. The skip label is the firmer prediction.
6. Tseitin hardness is asymptotic and about resolution on expanders. This solver has IALH, and C16(1,2) is tiny. No lower bound follows for this solver.
7. I have not seen canon_plus or elim_plus. Audit finding (b) is an estimate.
8. Finding (d) covers pure parity blocks only. Mixed formulas may differ.
mechanism_signature: KERNEL-SECTION + ORBIT-COVER | unimplemented, hand-derived | N = flip-closure group = (sum A_K)^perp | certificate: echelon generators, J, clause-lookup closure, no tables, no width cap | quotient = restriction x_J=0, r variables, no clause or width growth | greedy matroid choice of J | extra clauses: density sum 2^-rho < 1 implies redundancy, lifting by conditional expectations | v3 adapted basis kept as width optimiser | kernel-free residual untouched | residual solver unbounded
delta_from_prior:
00058 treated incompatible spaces as a frame-sparsity problem (T98) and reported no progress on extra clauses.

New here:
(1) An audit of the v3 code: soundness confirmed by reading, plus four findings (2^|K| verification factor, unbudgeted greedy cost, r=n rejection, exact parity blind spot).
(2) KERNEL-SECTION: the r-variable quotient always exists as a plain restriction with a table-free certificate.
(3) A correction to 00058: coordinate frames never increase clause count, so SPARSE-FRAME is not the obstruction to dimension reduction. Only width optimality remains (T102).
(4) ORBIT-COVER, the first positive, conditional extra-clause statement in this line.
(5) A 32-variable Tseitin control with exact v3 predictions.

Not new: LQC soundness, ATOM-REFINE, the NP-hardness of unconditional extra clauses. There is no result on kernel-free residuals and no universal bound.
